newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU foreign ministers to discuss Iraq, Middle East.
newsitem.headline: EU foreign ministers to discuss Iraq, Middle East.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers began arriving in the southern Irish town of Tralee on Saturday for an informal meeting to discuss the 15-nation bloc's policy on issues from Iraq to former Yugoslavia.
At the two-day meeting, the ministers were also expected to discuss a response to U.S. trade laws concerning Cuba, Iran and Libya that are widely opposed outside of Washington.

The failure of the bloc to agree a common position on America's attack on Iraq -- with Britain and Germany backing the move and France, Spain and Italy reserving support -- was expected to cause some discomfort at the meeting.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who was to host the meeting, told Irish radio he did not believe a common position could be found.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind called on his colleagues to support the United States or come up with a better plan for dealing with Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.
"We have not heard that alternative, and until we do I belive the U.S. deserves our full support," he told BBC radio.
Spring, meanwhile, has said he wants the main topic of the meeting to be focused on ways to help the Middle East peace process get back on track.
